findings.claim: The partial remove (uninstall kmctl's entry, then 'the normal install' for the harnesses kept) reinstalls at package_ref(), the running CLI's version, not the ref the removed entry pinned, so removing one harness silently upgrades or downgrades the one kept, and needs the network and that tag to exist on the source. If that reinstall fails (offline, dev build with no such tag, APM skip), the uninstall has already taken the kept harness's skills, rules and lock entry, so 'remove antigravity' leaves claude broken. The plan must say which ref the reinstall uses (the entry's or lock's resolved_ref) and what remove does when the reinstall fails.

Remove takes the removed harnesses out of apm.yml targets, but it cannot tell whether a target was there before kmctl added it (write_manifest only appends missing ones). A repo that already targeted claude for its own APM packages loses that target; spike:plugin-remove/2 shows that the next apm install with a target dropped cleans every package's files for that target, so the user's own packages vanish from .claude/ on their next apm install. That breaks the plan's own bar that other apm.yml entries stay untouched. The plan needs a rule, e.g. drop a target only when no other apm.yml entry remains, or leave targets when other entries exist and say so.

The uninstall identifier HOST/OWNER/REPO/apm was proved only for a host:port local server (spike:plugin-remove/1 lists the github form as untried). For the default source the lock has no host, so the plan builds github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm, which no spike or integration test (local git server only) exercises; if APM wants OWNER/REPO/apm there, uninstall aborts with 'not found in apm.yml' on every real install. Settle with a spike: after an install from https://github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management (or a lock with host unset), which identifier does apm 0.33.0 uninstall accept?
The kept harnesses are now reinstalled from the removed entry's git source and ref, and a failed reinstall refuses with exit 1, names APM's cause and the install command that puts them back.

A target is dropped only when no other dependencies.apm entry is left, and doctor's harnesses_found ignores targets when the lock lists kmctl's package, so a kept target neither wipes the user's packages nor marks a removed harness installed.
spike:plugin-remove/5 shows apm 0.33.0 uninstall accepts github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm for a GitHub-sourced entry and removes the entry and its packages.

The plan builds the uninstall name from the lock's host and repo_url, but spike:plugin-remove/5's lock shows APM lowercases repo_url for GitHub (repo_url jasperhg90/knowledge-management; the original case is only in materialization_repo_url), while the spike passed the mixed-case github.com/JasperHG90/Knowledge-management/apm by hand. So the name the plan would actually build, github.com/jasperhg90/knowledge-management/apm, is untested. If APM matches the apm.yml entry case-sensitively, remove aborts with 'not found' on every install from the default source, which spike 3 (an all-lowercase local server) cannot show. Settle with a spike: after the same GitHub install, does apm 0.33.0 uninstall --dry-run accept github.com/jasperhg90/knowledge-management/apm? If not, the plan should name materialization_repo_url, or the apm.yml entry's git URL, as the source of the name.

When none of the named harnesses is installed but another one is, the summary line says kmctl is not installed here. With claude installed, remove --harness antigravity prints 'kmctl is not installed here (project scope); removed nothing', which is false.

If apm uninstall fails during remove, or uvx is missing, the error comes from _require/_apm_run and ends with 'then kmctl plugin install again'. That is the wrong next step for remove: a human or agent who follows it puts kmctl back.
The `kmctl plugin` row of the commands table in docs/reference/commands.md still lists 'Verbs: install, update'. The help text now says install, update, remove.

The r3 test installs from DEFAULT_SOURCE, so a reinstall that ignored the entry's git: URL and used DEFAULT_SOURCE would still pass. Only the ref is pinned down. Use a non-default source, such as an http URL with a port, and assert the reinstalled entry's git.

entries.change: When nothing named is installed but another harness is, the summary says removed nothing and names the harness still installed.
_require, _apm and _apm_run take the verb to rerun; remove's uninstall and claude mcp remove pass kmctl plugin remove, so their errors no longer say to run install again.
The kmctl plugin row lists install, update and remove.
The reinstall test installs from a mirror URL and checks the uninstall name and the source kept; new tests check the summary line and that a failed uninstall names remove.

findings.claim: the summary line said kmctl was not installed when another harness was still installed
remove's APM and claude failures told the reader to run kmctl plugin install again
the commands.md row for kmctl plugin did not list remove among its verbs
the r3 test did not pin the source of the reinstall
